title: Choose your project
concept: Planning · a brief before the build
description: Pick your final project, from a word game to a full app, and plan it: who it is for, what it must do, and what waits.

tasks.title: Plan it before you build it
tasks.body: Your final project is a program you plan and build yourself. There are three, from smaller to larger: Lockpick, a word-guessing game; Site Builder, which turns a data file into a small website; and Planner, a to-do app that keeps your plan. Pick the one that stretches you without stopping you.
tasks.detail: A brief says what you will build before you build it: who it is for, what it must do, and what it will not do yet. The not-yet list matters most, because it keeps the project small enough to finish. Milestones split the work into pieces you can run and show.

tasks.code:
# A brief, kept as Python data
brief = {
    "project": "Lockpick",
    "for": "my brother, who likes word games",
    "must": [
        "guess one letter at a time",
        "six misses and the lock jams",
        "play again",
    ],
    "not yet": ["hints", "two players"],
}
print(brief["project"], "for", brief["for"])
for feature in brief["must"]:
    print("-", feature)
print("Not yet:", ", ".join(brief["not yet"]))
tasks.output:
Lockpick for my brother, who likes word games
- guess one letter at a time
- six misses and the lock jams
- play again
Not yet: hints, two players
tasks.note: The brief is a dictionary, with one key for each part of the plan. The not-yet list is printed last, so it is clear what the first version leaves out.

tasks.question: Which belongs on the not-yet list for a first version of Lockpick?
options: A hint that costs a try
Showing the word as _ a _ _ t
tasks.why: The other two are what make it Lockpick at all. A hint is an extra: good to have, but the game works without it.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: add a third item to "not yet", and change "for" to someone you might show your project to. Then add a "milestones" list with three steps, and print each one on its own line.

Choose one project and write its brief. Lockpick: a word game where six wrong letters jam the lock (one file, 6 to 8 hours, a good first big program). Site Builder: turns a data file into a small website (10 to 15 hours, after unit 10). Planner: a to-do app that remembers your plan (several files, 20 to 30 hours, after every unit). Signed in, your recorded brief comes back here each time you open this lesson.
hints: Choose by what you finished, not by what sounds biggest: a small project that works beats a large one that does not.
A milestone is something you can run and show, like "the word shows as underscores" or "one page is written". "Finish the code" is not a milestone.
For the not-yet list, think of the first extra you would add after it works. That is the one to leave out for now.

criteria.text: I chose one of the three projects.
criteria.ask: Which one, and why does it suit you right now?

criteria.text: I named who it is for.
criteria.ask: Who will use it, and what do they want from it?

criteria.text: I listed what it must do.
criteria.ask: List three to five things it must do.

criteria.text: I listed what it will not do yet.
criteria.ask: What are you leaving out of the first version?

criteria.text: I split it into milestones I can run.
criteria.ask: What are your first three milestones, each something you can run and show?
